# R333 — persistent Prefill allocation owners and state aliases

Date: 2026-10-13 (JST). Read-only source audit at W HEAD 4d0fb23095742615c698147cbe4212211a1b181f. Consulted registry v177 (850 reports), R321/R322 and implementation-phase-decode-cache-growth-source-v1 for lifecycle context. No source edit, build, test, import, project execution, GPU/process/profiler work, Git mutation, cleanup, active record access, or in-flight implementation packet inspection. This ledger is source-grounded only; no actual allocated or freed byte total was measured.

## Finding

Persistent serve initializes one Prefill object before READY. Its read_part/read_windows path reuses that object for prompts, then the request decodes through persistent Verifier and SessionState owners while Prefill workspace remains allocated. The next GEN uses Prefill again. After a completed prompt, only Prefill-owned resources can be retired; QSA KV, GDN recurrent state, PLE sequence history, verifier state, cache and residency bindings must survive. Before a following prompt reaches sp.run, Prefill must be initialized again against the still-live engine state.

An owner omitted from R322 is Gemm's lazy BF16-to-FP16 fallback buffers tc_w and tc_x. They are device allocations owned by the Gemm member inside Prefill::Impl, outside Impl::owned and Prefill::bytes_needed. When the device/path takes the FP16-only matrix fallback, tc_w grows to the largest N*K weight projection in u16 elements; tc_x grows to min(T,16Mi/K)*K u16 elements (16Mi elements max). They may be tens or hundreds of MiB depending on projection dimensions; actual target allocation is unmeasured and the path may not use them. Prefill::reset replaces Impl, whose Gemm destructor frees them after release has drained compute. A plan that counts only owned or calls only the release helper misses this owner.

## Persistent serve lifecycle

Serve creates sp, calls init before request handling, and uses the same object through read_part. Prompt completion includes existing slot refill/residency publication and cpu_jobs.finish, then decode runs on the persistent verifier/session. Prefill run mutates SessionState sequence data, not just private scratch. A successful run ends with compute-stream synchronization; reset drains compute and copy streams, cancels and destroys the stager and events, then frees owned device pointers. Retirement is eligible only after successful prompt completion, callback completion, queue drains, and no batch/interleaved prompt work.

Reset clears PrefillStats, so preserve needed stats first. It leaves Prefill empty. Before the next GEN calls run, reinitialize with the current WeightTable, geometry, SessionState, expert source/cache/residency map, chunk and compute stream. Reestablish request-specific callbacks and stage/image settings. For the constrained no-MTP/no-borrow single-device case, borrow is null, there is no lent-slot refill or MTP on_chunk callback, and cache/residency remain unchanged. This resets only scratch; preserve the session state and context.

## Allocation ledger and aliases

Alloc::take<T>(n) requests round to (n*sizeof(T)+256+255)&~255 bytes. With no borrow, each take becomes a separate device allocation listed in Impl::owned. With a borrowed cache region, take returns a bump pointer into that cache span; it is an alias and must not be freed separately. Source formulas are raw element counts; alignment overhead applies per allocation.

- Dense GEMM scratch: 32Mi u16 elements, 64 MiB raw. The first owned allocation; Gemm.scratch aliases it via init_external.
- Chunk planes: emb T*N f32; R T*D f32; xn T*HC f32; xn16 T*D u16; lo T*LR f32 and lo16 T*LR u16; gated T*D f32; inj T*HC f32; mixed T*N f32; mixed_bf and mixed_h T*N u16; bo T*N f32. BF16X2 flags add low-part xn16 T*D, lo16 T*LR, and/or mixed_bf T*N u16. steps_dev is T*kStepCount i32. Here T is chunk, N is embedding width, D=hc*N, HC is stream count, LR is low-rank width.
- Shared region: one allocation of max(GDN set, QSA set, MoE set). These layouts overlay because their layer phases run serially; subregions are aliases into region.
- GDN overlay: qkv T*C, z T*ZV, ab T*2*HV, gate/beta T*HV, hbuf T*C, y T*ZV f32 and y_h T*ZV u16. This is scratch; recurrent state is in SessionState.
- QSA overlay: Kc,Vc T*512; Qf T*12288; q T*ZV; idx_raw T*128; q_idx T*512; attn T*ZV f32; attn_h T*ZV u16; sel_ids T*cap i32; sel_scores sel_batch*max_blocks f32; attn_scratch attn_batch*qsa_decode_attn_scratch_floats(cap,s) f32. cap is qsa_selection_width(kTopkMaxCells,s); max_blocks is SessionState QSA max_cells / index block + 2; sel_batch=256 and attn_batch=32 by current Impl defaults. The authoritative QSA KV pools/maps remain SessionState-owned.
- MoE overlay: logits T*n_expert f32; w T*K f32; ids/slot_dev/src_dev T*K i32; GU scratch_rows*1280 f32; Dm T*K*N f32; sgate/sup T*640 f32 each; sh_h T*640 u16; shared T*N and sg T f32; optional Xs/Hh activation u16 planes. scratch_rows is T only for guarded compact pure-FP16 fallback, otherwise T*K. MMQ adds q8 Xq/Hq and H=T*K*640 f32; exact allocations depend on runtime MMQ format plan.
- Other owned GPU buffers: dq_gu=G*1280*2560 u16 and dq_d=G*2560*640 u16 when FP16 fallback is needed (G defaults to 16); xb_dev=n_expert+1 i32; conditional compact bounds; conditional MMQ row identity/bounds, group buffers or two-group ring; ple_emb=T*N f32 and ple_norm=NG_HC_DIM f32. With no borrow, the expert staging ring is one allocation of ring*MMQ_SLOT and each stage_dev[i] aliases its interior. With a borrowed cache region, each stage_dev slot is carved from the cache region as MAXBLOB bytes. Separately, the short-chunk MMQ path can allocate an additional MMQ_RING*MMQ_SLOT mring buffer. ring_slots(T) is chunk-, blob-, pin-share-, memory- and env-dependent; T<2048 uses STAGE=8; larger chunks use selected 16..1024 slots. This ring can be a large chunk-scaled allocation.
- KV streaming helpers are conditional on SessionState qsa primary kv_mode==1. ident_table is n_pages i32. KvHostPools bytes use rows=n_pages*n_head_kv*page_size; int8 mode uses K/V int8 and K/V u16 scales, q4/hybrid modes have their own types. With STRATA_KV_STAGE_OWN, tables/pools are in owned storage; otherwise they are taken from the common layout and can alias a borrow. These are prompt staging helpers, not the persistent KV.
- Host/event resources: tok_host=T i32; steps_host=T*kStepCount; route HostVecs ids/slot/src=T*K, cnt=n_expert and off=n_expert+1; PLE double buffers T*N f32 pinned or pageable with per-buffer T*PLE_N_HEADS rows; copied/used events up to RING_MAX, two MMQ events, two PLE events and optional CPU-share events; a copy stream and Stager workers. Stager has STRATA_STAGER_RING (default 16, clamped 2..256) host slots of MAXBLOB bytes, DMA events and worker threads. These consume host/pinned memory, not VRAM.
- Conditional host buffers: CPU-share cpu_x grows to T*N*f32; cpu_rows grows with headroom to about 2*rows_cpu*N*f32; activation/job vectors accompany it. Layer-split nonfinal stages allocate two host handoff buffers of chunk*D*4 bytes. These are absent in the specified CPU-share-off, single-device route. MTP callbacks and drafter allocations have separate owners.
- Separate Gemm fallback owner: tc_w=max-NK u16 and tc_x=min(T,16Mi/K)*K u16 elements. These are lazy and reused across projections, not in owned/bytes_needed. The Gemm destructor owns their release.

The alias boundaries matter: Gemm scratch points into the first owned take; region subbuffers overlap one parent allocation; stage_dev may alias a ring base or borrowed cache bytes. Never free those interior pointers separately. Prefill has no persistent command-graph capture of these temporary buffers in the inspected source. Verifier/token graphs are separate and must remain valid.

## Owners that must survive

SessionState owns full-context QSA KV/state arenas and maps, QSA decode buffers, GDN recurrence/conv state, block/MoE/session arenas, residual R, PLE history and predecessor token fields. Prefill updates this sequence state but does not own it.

Verifier and any secondary verifiers own decode-window scratch, head/logit and nonfinite buffers, cache-offset tables and graph references. They remain live between requests. ExpertCache mappings, device/host residency tables, immutable source weights, model heads, PLE tables/weights, penalty history and pool are also separate owners. Do not recreate session/verifier or alter context/KV limits to retire Prefill scratch. The Prefill KV stage pool and identity map do not replace authoritative SessionState K/V.

## Next-GEN lifecycle contract

Only after a successful prompt and completion of all Prefill callbacks, producer work, copy/stager/issuer activity, slot refill and residency publication: snapshot stats, drain/reset sp, and retire Prefill-owned resources. Decode proceeds with the same SessionState/Verifier and cache mappings. Before the next GEN's prompt read, call sp.init with the live persistent objects/settings. Do not call sp.run while empty. If reset or prior prompt completion is uncertain, retain workspace and fail closed. If a later GEN reuses/restores a session, reset/reinit only the transient workspace and preserve that session's state.

R322 already covers the need for a serialized Prefill reset/reinit transition and cache/verifier owner coordination. R333 adds the detailed owners/aliases and Gemm's lazy allocations; it does not repeat the cache growth design. bytes_needed is a layout/preflight count, not a measurement of memory returned to the driver; it omits the lazy Gemm fallback and host/dynamic resources. Include Gemm high-water buffers in memory admission or measure a future drained before/after delta. Do not claim freed bytes or general FP16 equivalence from these formulas.
